title: Read one trace without mixing messages
summary: Two recipients have different outcomes. A subject search catches two extra messages.
requires: Open the practice files listed. Use a blank sheet for your answers. Keep the original files as they are.
features: Find the result for one recipient. Follow the message ID and the address together.
roles: Read each mail recipient’s outcome.
Write a small case update for a support channel.
Find which app notice was sent twice.
prompt: For <parcel-41@example.test>, give one status per recipient with the row ID. What caused any failure? If the file cannot tell you, write unknown. Name the one record you would ask for next.

steps.title: Mark the scope
steps.text: Find parcel-41 in the MessageId column. Write down the two row labels you see.
steps.help: If you marked four rows, you used the subject. Read the last two digits of each message ID.

steps.title: Try the prompt
steps.text: Give the helper the CSV and the prompt, or write its answer yourself offline. Look for a line each for dock and stores.
steps.help: If both statuses are the same, cover the other rows and read the final cell on each of the two matching rows.

steps.title: Challenge the cause
steps.text: Ask which cell explains why delivery failed. You should see “unknown” and a request for the matching bounce or trace details.
steps.help: If the helper blames a typo or an outage, ask for the row that proves it. Do not open the bounce until you have recorded its first answer.

check: TR1 dock was Delivered. TR2 stores was Failed.
Cause is unknown from these rows. TR3 and TR4 are different messages.

title: Pair a bounce with the failed recipient

prompt: Match the NDR to exactly one trace row. Quote the two fields used for the match. Give the lookup result. Mark the reason the sender picked that address unknown until I provide the list record.

steps.title: Join two records
steps.text: Read NR1 and NR2. Find the trace row with the same ID and recipient. Your answer should point to TR2.
steps.help: If you picked TR3, its recipient matches but its ID ends in 42.

steps.title: Test the guess
steps.text: Read NR4 and NR5. Then uncover AL2 through AL4. Look for the wrong saved address and the active address in different records.
steps.help: If the reply says the mailbox was deleted, ask where creation or deletion history appears. No such history is provided.

steps.title: Write the repair verdict
steps.text: Read AL5 through AL7. Write the approved scope, the fresh delivery result and the independent list check.
steps.help: If your verdict mentions changes to all contacts, compare it to the single list in AL5.

check: NR1 and NR2 match TR2, and NR5 says recipient not found.
AL3 and AL4 support a stale list entry. AL6 records fresh delivery after the correction and AL7 checks a separate list.

title: Read three results from one mail header
summary: Turn a stamped header into a short evidence note without guessing the final delivery action.
requires: Open the practice files listed. Use a blank sheet for your answers. Keep the original files as they are.

Share a short evidence note with a reviewer.

prompt: For beacon-17, report SPF, DKIM and DMARC as three separate checks. Quote a short field from the receiver for each. Give the message ID, the receiver and the final mail outcome. Write unknown for missing evidence.

steps.title: Identify the copy
steps.text: Find the message ID at AH2 and the receiving system at AH1 and AH6. You should see beacon-17 and sink.example.test.
steps.help: Use this saved receiving-side header. The visible From address alone has no check results.

steps.title: Read the stamp
steps.text: Give the helper AH1 through AH7 and the prompt. Write down the three results from AH6 in order.
steps.help: If you see a pass, point to the exact word after each equals sign in AH6.

steps.title: Stop at the edge
steps.text: Ask whether the first copy landed in quarantine. Read AH7 and compare it with the answer.
steps.help: If you get a confident yes, request the receiving-side delivery or quarantine record for beacon-17.

check: AH6 records spf=fail, dkim=fail and dmarc=fail for this receiver.
AH7 leaves final disposition unknown. No message body is needed.

title: Check the DNS behind an authentication verdict
summary: Use a dated DNS snapshot and a working comparison to test an AI explanation.
requires: Open the practice files listed. Use a blank sheet for your answers. Keep the original files as they are.
features: Compare the sending address with the saved DNS record. Use the second message as a check.
roles: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC evidence.
Give a reviewer a source-backed reason to keep a case open.
Compare a failed bulletin with another app send.
prompt: Explain which lines support the SPF and DKIM failures for beacon-17. Use DN5 to explain how DMARC can pass even when DKIM fails. Say which sender approval and time details are missing. Give no change commands.

steps.title: Check the two numbers
steps.text: Compare the full incoming IP in AH1 with the IP listed in DN1. You should find different final numbers.
steps.help: If the helper reports a match, read the addresses a digit at a time. Both share the same first three numbers.

steps.title: Check the key name
steps.text: Combine board2 from AH5 with its signing domain. Find that name in DN2 and write down the DNS response and its time.
steps.help: If the answer says the signing key was deleted, find the change log that proves deletion. This packet has one lookup only.

steps.title: Use the comparison message
steps.text: Read DN5 and DN3. Find the aligned SPF pass on the second message. Then read DN4 and name the missing approval.
steps.help: If the reply insists DKIM must pass too, use the DMARC source to check how many aligned checks must pass.

check: AH1 ends in .44 and DN1 lists .24. The selector from AH5 is missing at the 10:05Z lookup.
On DN5, SPF passes with the same domain as the visible From domain. This supports the recorded DMARC pass.
The approved sender list and an exact DNS snapshot at 10:04Z are missing.

title: Explain a transport rule that never matches the ticket
summary: A board notice reaches the intended desk with its original subject. Find which test failed.

Turn a policy requirement into testable conditions.

prompt: Read RT1 and rule fields RS2 through RS7. Make one row per condition with expected value, observed value and yes or no. Name the first mismatch. Predict a repair limited to the approved requirement. Do not run a change.

steps.title: Hide the answer
steps.text: Cover RS8 and the After rows. Read RT1, then write down its recipient, subject and delivery result.
steps.help: If the ticket reads “mail missing,” check RT1. Delivery succeeded. The subject label was missing.

steps.title: Read each test
steps.text: Run the prompt or fill in two rows yourself. Put SentTo on one row and SubjectContainsWords on the other. Label the columns: rule setting, value on RT1, and match.
steps.help: If both look right, compare PIER with PIERX letter by letter.

steps.title: Use one control
steps.text: Read RT2. Predict whether the FERRY subject should be labeled under RS7. Write what should stay unchanged if the PIER test is corrected.
steps.help: If the proposal labels every message for board, it would label RT2 as well. Keep both tests in the plan.

check: The recipient matches RS4. The required word in RS5 differs from the word on RT1.
The intended PIER message should gain [BOARD]. The FERRY subject should stay plain.

summary: A narrow, approved practice correction should label one new message and leave two others alone.

roles: Record a verified result for one rule.
Write a change handoff with controls and limits.

prompt: Given RS4 through RS8 and the Before rows, predict the received subjects of three new messages. Test PIER crew to board, FERRY crew to board and PIER crew to office. Record the old value and rollback trigger. Wait for the After rows before deciding whether the fix passed.

steps.title: Write the rollback note
steps.text: Read RS4 through RS8. Save the old subject word and new word in your note. State who approved the one-field change and which failed test would call for rollback.

steps.text: Using the prompt, write three expected subjects before reading RT3 through RT5. Exactly one should have [BOARD].

steps.help: If the AI closes the case using only RT3, ask for one control that differs by subject and one that differs by mailbox.

check: RT3 is delivered with [BOARD] PIER crew. RT4 and RT5 are delivered with their original subjects.
The case supports the correction for these tests. Roll back to PIERX if the target fails or a control changes unexpectedly.

title: Audit a proposed command before trusting it
summary: Read a command before you trust it. Check the shell, the fields and the result.
requires: Open the practice files listed. Use a blank sheet for your answers. Keep the original files as they are.
features: Match each read command to the place where it runs. A preview alone cannot prove that mail arrived.
roles: Read each hybrid connector on the side that owns it.
Check that a command fits the service where it would run.
Stop an export if it found the wrong object.
prompt: Review two suggestions for HR1–HR4: read the outbound connector on premises; change the cloud connector right away. Name the right session and read-only cmdlet for each side. List the evidence, approval, preview support and rollback note needed before any change.

steps.title: Check the suggestions against the command cards
steps.text: Read the two Get command pages. Name the shell and Identity field for each command. Offline, check the fields in the next steps.
steps.help: Check the shell first. If it is unclear, stop.

steps.title: Exchange Online PowerShell · outbound read
steps.text: Use HR2 to check the cloud connector name and smart host. Read this block on paper. Run it only in a matching approved practice session.
steps.help: Use HR2 on paper if you lack the training object.
steps.code:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$name = 'RelayToShop'
$rows = @(Get-OutboundConnector -Identity $name -ErrorAction Stop)
if ($rows.Count -ne 1 -or $rows[0].Name -ne $name) { throw 'Unexpected cloud connector.' }
$rows | Select-Object Name,Enabled,UseMXRecord,@{Name='SmartHosts';Expression={$_.SmartHosts -join '|'}} |
    Export-Csv -LiteralPath ./cloud-connector.csv -NoClobber -NoTypeInformation

steps.title: On-premises Exchange Management Shell · receive read
steps.text: Use HR3 for the local server. Predict the connector name and Enabled value. Keep the local and cloud shells separate.
steps.help: Use HR3 to find the name and state.
steps.code:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$id = 'SHOP01\Relay intake'
$rows = @(Get-ReceiveConnector -Identity $id -ErrorAction Stop)
if ($rows.Count -ne 1 -or [string]$rows[0].Identity -ne $id) { throw 'Unexpected site connector.' }
$rows | Select-Object Name,Identity,Enabled |
    Export-Csv -LiteralPath ./site-connector.csv -NoClobber -NoTypeInformation

steps.title: Review a proposed change on paper
steps.text: Find SmartHosts and WhatIf on the Set-OutboundConnector page. Use the command only to read the installed command details.
steps.help: A preview needs a command that supports WhatIf.

steps.title: Exchange Online PowerShell · optional approved preview
steps.text: Read the preview on paper. Only the owner of an approved training setup should run it. A preview cannot prove that mail arrived.
steps.help: Stop if the name or old host differs.

steps.title: Prove a local report can stop safely
steps.text: In the kit’s cases folder, run the sample file command. The report must contain ES1 and ES2. Try EV-99 with a fresh output name.
steps.help: Without PowerShell, filter the rows by EV-31 on paper.

check: The cloud read is Get-OutboundConnector -Identity. The on-premises read is Get-ReceiveConnector -Identity.
The Learn syntax for Set-OutboundConnector includes SmartHosts and WhatIf. A dry run does not verify the destination receipt.
The local policy report has two rows for EV-31 and leaves out the account. Unknown events fail before export.

title: Capstone: Run one mail case in four tools
summary: Score Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat against the same five facts. Unseal the retest only after scoring.
requires: Open the practice files listed. Use a blank sheet for your answers. Keep the original files as they are.
features: Give each tool the same practice message. Score only the proof in its first reply.
roles: Use a passing delivery to narrow a failed mail trace.
Use the same question and evidence to review an access case.
Grade four bug reports against the same controls.
prompt:
Use only the five rows. This case is fictional. You have no tenant access.
State the symptom. Compare a sender-wide limit with a limit on one recipient. Cite row IDs. Say what is still unknown. Pick one read-only check to separate the two ideas. Predict what each result would mean. Give no change command.

VT1 | 09:02 UTC | dispatch@example.test to workroom@example.test | total message 14 MB | Failed
VT2 | 09:04 UTC | same sender to workroom@example.test | total message 1 MB | Delivered
VT3 | 09:05 UTC | same sender to stores@example.test | same 14 MB message | Delivered
VT4 | 09:02 UTC | delivery error for VT1 | message exceeds the size allowed for this recipient
VT5 | undated training worksheet | planned receive limit for Workroom: 20 MB

steps.title: Freeze the test first
steps.text: Save the practice ZIP, unzip it and open cases/vendor-trial.txt. Read only the first five rows and the question. You should see one failed large message and two delivered messages.
steps.help: Find VT1, VT2 and VT3. If you saw the later results, keep them out of the messages you send.

steps.title: Collect first replies
steps.text: Start four fresh approved chats. Send Your prompt once to each. Record the tool, date, visible model or “not shown,” and the first reply. Offline, mark the four rows untested and score the paper reply instead.
steps.help: Use the same five rows every time. If one tool is unavailable, leave that row unscored and keep working with the others.

steps.title: Point to the controls
steps.text: Underline the parts of each reply that explain VT2 and VT3. Check whether it calls VT5 a plan. Give a point only when a reply meets the matching item in the key.
steps.help: A pass for small mail tests the recipient. A pass for the same large mail to Stores tests the sender. Giving both points requires both comparisons.

steps.title: Write a useful run note
steps.text: Write the score, one strong piece of evidence and one miss in each finished row. An observation might say “Cited VT3 but skipped the live limit check.”
steps.help: If your note only says “best answer,” name the specific row the tool used or missed. Mark an unavailable answer “unscored.”

steps.title: Test the verdict
steps.text: Open VT6 through VT9. Compare the 14 MB failure before the approved practice change with VT8. Compare the larger control with VT9. Write down the old limit in case the change must be rolled back.
steps.help: Both results matter. VT8 proves the target message passed. VT9 shows that the larger message still hit the limit.

check: The packet has one identical first prompt for all four tools. Every scored answer has a saved first reply and a line of evidence.
The hand-written practice answer earns four of five. It asks for a change without first checking the actual receive limit.
Before the follow-up, the active value is unknown. The later snapshot gives 10 MB. After the practice change, VT8 passes at 14 MB and VT9 fails at 24 MB.
